title: Global Scientist Interdisciplinary Forum • Autumn 2026  - Shenzhen, Guangdong, China job with Southern University of Science and Technology, School of Medicine | 12864407
gist: This is a faculty-recruitment job posting, not a research paper: Southern University of Science and Technology (SUSTech) in Shenzhen is running an Autumn 2026 'Global Scientist Interdisciplinary Forum' to hire senior and junior medical/public-health faculty, offering tax rebates, housing, and immigration support, and disclosing rapid research-output growth at its young medical school.

insights.claim: SUSTech's School of Medicine and School of Public Health and Emergency Management are jointly running a 'Global Scientist Interdisciplinary Forum' in autumn 2026 in Shenzhen specifically as a talent-recruitment event to fill Senior Faculty (Chair Professor/Professor) and Junior Faculty (Associate/Assistant Professor) positions.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
entities: Southern University of Science and Technology
insights.so_what: Illustrates China's continued proactive, event-based approach to recruiting international biomedical scientists even amid broader US-China science-talent tensions.

insights.claim: Recruitment incentives include a globally competitive salary, income-tax compensation from the local government of up to 15% for highly qualified individuals, Shenzhen's highest tier of retirement/medical/unemployment/injury/maternity insurance, on-campus or subsidized housing, and permanent residence or resident visa services for scholars and their families.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
entities: Southern University of Science and Technology
insights.so_what: This is a concrete benchmark of the fiscal and immigration incentives Chinese municipalities are offering to compete for global scientific talent, useful for comparing against Western university/government recruitment packages.

insights.claim: As of August 2026, SUSTech's School of Medicine, including its affiliated hospitals, had published 5,417 articles and secured 741 grants totaling over 736 million yuan (roughly $100 million), despite the university being founded only around 14 years earlier (2012).
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
entities: Southern University of Science and Technology
insights.so_what: Quantifies how quickly a Chinese medical school can scale research output and grant funding, evidence of the speed of state-backed institution-building in Chinese biomedicine.

insights.claim: 58% of the School of Medicine's 226 full-time faculty hold national, provincial, or municipal 'talent titles,' indicating heavy reliance on China's state talent-recognition programs to staff a young research institution.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
entities: Southern University of Science and Technology
insights.so_what: A majority-talent-title faculty base signals the institution's research capacity is substantially built through state talent-recruitment programs rather than organic faculty growth.

themes.theme: AI and public health as an explicit hiring priority

insights.claim: SUSTech's School of Public Health and Emergency Management, founded in April 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic jointly with the Shenzhen Center for Disease Control and Prevention, is explicitly recruiting scholars in the application of big data and artificial intelligence in public health, alongside precision medicine, epidemiology, and infectious-disease control.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
entities: Southern University of Science and Technology
Shenzhen Center for Disease Control and Prevention
insights.so_what: Shows China converting pandemic-era urgency into a permanent institutional focus that explicitly names AI-in-public-health as a strategic hiring priority, relevant to tracking China's AI-health research investment.
